recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5196 unless PA later decides to revise Encounter participant or PractitionerRole modeling guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-5196 was a Published PA ballot issue with Not Persuasive with Modification resolution asking for clarification around Encounter participant type versus Practitioner roles. The resolution directed adding a comment that Encounter participant type describes how an actor participates in the specific encounter, including non-practitioners and context roles such as Admitting Dr or Consulting Dr, while practitioner roles are functional roles derived from employment, education, licensing, and similar authority.
initial_application: Historical commit 27302910ae49c6d1fd5544682e5f48f9e365b347 explicitly listed tracker 5196 and added the requested comment to the Encounter spreadsheet source. Subsequent source migration preserved the text in source/encounter/structuredefinition-Encounter.xml.
additional_context: Encounter is active and approved in source/fhir.ini. Later FHIR-22696 work renamed Encounter.participant.individual to Encounter.participant.actor and adjusted the comment to say individual actor, but preserved the FHIR-5196 distinction. Current PractitionerRole source remains consistent by defining PractitionerRole.code as roles a practitioner is authorized to perform for an organization. Community searches found no FHIR-5196-specific Zulip or Confluence conflict; a related implementers thread supports the same modeling distinction.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/encounter/structuredefinition-Encounter.xml already includes the requested clarification at Encounter.participant.type and the relevant source is in current build scope.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied/Published Encounter participant work renamed individual to actor and updated the wording from individual to individual actor without changing the FHIR-5196 role distinction.
